Whether one Forget covers two Major gains
Whether an ordinarily forgotten Unique can be reclaimed
answers.answer: A gifted/transferred Major does not require Forgetting, unlike gaining one. Each Major gained requires its own separate Forget. A forgotten Unique goes under its Spirit panel and is unavailable to ordinary Reclaim or gain.

evidence.text: An effect that **gifts/transfers** a Major, or explicitly says to **take** one without Forgetting, differs from gaining it. A gain still requires Forgetting unless explicitly exempted. Follow the effect's wording. Cards gained enter hand unless explicitly placed elsewhere. Gaining during Growth allows playing that card in the later play/pay step; gaining it mid-turn does not by itself let you play it. Gaining a card does not itself resolve that card's effects.

After **gaining a Major**, Forget one of your cards permanently. You may Forget from hand, personal discard, or play, including the Major just gained. A forgotten Minor/Major goes to its shared deck discard; a forgotten Unique goes under its Spirit panel, unavailable to ordinary Reclaim or gain. If you Forget from play, immediately lose its Elements and any unused activation; an already resolved effect persists normally. Each Major gained requires its own Forget; a single card cannot satisfy separate Forget requirements.

requested_parts: When Gift of Strength or Powerstorm Repeat target is chosen
Whether a Slow card can be repeated
Whether an innate can be repeated by those permissions
Whether printed card Elements are gained again
answers.answer: For Gift of Strength and Powerstorm, choose an eligible card when you actually Repeat it, and it may be a card played later that turn. It may be Slow, but these permissions repeat Power Cards, not Innates. A Repeat gives no additional printed card Elements.

evidence.text: Retain changes to the Power, including extra Range or changed speed. An ordinary Repeat uses the Power's **most recently assigned speed**: a Slow Power repeats in Slow even if its permission came from a Fast Power; a formerly Fast Power explicitly made Slow before repeating now repeats in Slow. An instruction to Repeat immediately instead follows that explicit timing, directly after the originating use. [FAQ repeating-powers-with-changed-speeds] You may postpone choosing which eligible card to repeat until you actually repeat it, and make different choices/targets then. For **Powerstorm** and **Gift of Strength**, the Spirit receives a once-this-turn option rather than a grant-time selection of cards: a card played later that turn may be selected while it remains in play, subject to the permission’s restrictions and cost. [FAQ timing-of-choosing-powers-for-once-this-turn-repeats] Gift of Strength imposes its printed card-cost eligibility ceiling but requires no additional Energy payment for the Repeat, so an eligible card may be repeated with no Energy left. If the permission requires paying a cost, pay it as instructed. **Powerstorm** requires paying the repeated Power Card's Energy cost again when exercising each Repeat, including its threshold's further permissions; the original play payment does not cover it.

- **Repeat limits:** **Powerstorm** and **Gift of Strength** repeat Power **Cards**, not Innates. Powerstorm's threshold repeats up to three **different** cards. A Range/Speed change granted by a threshold carries to a Repeat even if that threshold is no longer met; it does not stack the same Range bonus again.
